name: Sprites (Fly.io)

modes.label: Sprite, billed on actual CPU time + actual memory while awake
modes.note: Every Sprite has 8 vCPU; CPU billed on cumulative cpu.stat CPU time, memory on actual usage (platform-managed, ~8 GB cap in practice). Hot storage $0.000683/GB-h on bytes written only while awake (extra key disk_gib_h_running). Warm (~30 s idle) and cold states bill no CPU/RAM/hot storage. Granularity: 'metered per hour of active use', exact rounding unpublished. Region not selectable. [basis verified 2026-09-28] fly.io/pricing: CPU "Cumulative CPU usage measured by cpu.stat" $0.07/CPU-hour; memory "Actual memory usage" $0.04375/GB-hour; "Sprites have three states: running (billed), warm (not billed), and cold (not billed)"; idle window ~30 s (docs.fly.io/sprites/concepts/lifecycle). No minimum/floor published. Whether page cache counts in "actual memory usage" is not stated (likely cgroup memory, which includes cache - unverified); "billed hourly" rounding unpublished.

knobs.label: Share of session the Sprite is awake (not warm/cold)
knobs.why: A Sprite goes warm ~30 s after last activity; warm and cold states bill no CPU, RAM or hot storage (cold storage continues). Anything that keeps it awake (open TCP connection to its URL, stdout output, a held Tasks API call) keeps RAM billing. Default 1 = awake the whole session.

caveats: Pricing section says 'No plans and no tiers' while the FAQ on the same page (and Fly's 2026-09-09 article) describe optional plans; Hero $100 is confirmed current. Other tier prices/allowances come from the 2026-01-16 community post; the 2026-01-22 release note listed a different set (Recruit free, Adventurer $20, Legend $200, Mythic $2,000).

Plan fee is NOT credit: it buys per-resource unit allowances (CPU-h, RAM GB-h, storage GB-month) that are not fungible (Fly staff post 2026-01-16: "Usage beyond included amounts is billed at standard usage-based rates"). Encoded as included_cpu_h / included_ram_gib_h / included_storage_gib_month on each plan with included_usd 0, so the engine (which only knows a fungible included_usd) never credits unused CPU hours against RAM overage; until the engine consumes the buckets, plans are never auto-picked over PAYG and the PAYG price is an upper bound for heavy users. Fly account credits cannot pay plan fees.

Storage: disk_gib_month 0.02 is COLD storage on all bytes written, billed for as long as kept (including while awake). HOT storage $0.000683/GB-h ($0.50/GB-mo) additionally bills on the awake working set (mode key disk_gib_h_running). Checkpoint storage not priced separately; snapshot_gib_month 0.02 assumes checkpoints are billed as cold storage (unverified).
Memory is billed on actual usage; the engine's ram_util drives the bill. RAM cap ~8 GB in practice (16 GB advertised, 'not available yet' per Jan 2026 support reply). max_ram_gib 8.
Fixed shape: 8 vCPU, 100 GB filesystem ceiling, one managed Ubuntu image (no custom image), no region selection, no public IPv4/SSH.

FUTURE TARIFF (not yet applied; today 2026-09-28): effective 2026-10-01 CPU $0.03825/CPU-h and memory $0.021875/GB-h (fly.io/pricing-update; vendor example 2 CPU + 4 GB for 720 h: $226.80 -> $118.08). Storage rates unchanged. Card keeps current $0.07 / $0.04375 until then; the dollar value of plan allowances will roughly halve too.
Rates history: 2025-12-30 RAM $0.011/GB-h and storage $0.10/GB-mo; current RAM $0.04375 (~4x higher; change date not found).
PAYG running-concurrency cap unpublished (concurrency null). Limits return errors, never extra charges.
No benchmark data in benchmarks.json (perf null); docs claim warm resume 100-500 ms, cold wake 1-2 s.
